name: lame-3d-revolve-tet10
reference: Benchmark D6. The same Lame thick cylinder as lame-3d-revolve-hex20 (a = 0.1 m, b = 0.2 m, internal pressure p = 60 MPa, E = 200 GPa, nu = 0.3), but the tube is a 90-degree CSG revolve (geometry.add) tagged tube.zmin/outer/zmax/inner by segment and tube.theta0/theta1 on the cut faces -- the identical Set names the hex20 case's mapped block gives the sweep mesher -- meshed by the free tet mesher instead of sweep+mapped. Order 2 gives tet10 with mid-edge nodes projected onto the curved inner and outer faces by isosurface stuffing (ADR 0021), so the boundary is round rather than faceted. This row's own reaction-balance and freshness checks (below) are the gate: the model is well posed and the tube.* Sets a sweep-mesher Journal already relies on still resolve after mesh.set swaps the mesher, the point #22 exists to prove. Point-probed stress and displacement at r = 0.15 m (mid-wall) are recorded, not gated: this mesher's dihedral-bounded cut-and-warp tetrahedra converge on a point value far more slowly than the sweep mesher's exact prismatic hex20 do (13% stress / 13% displacement error even at h = 0.012 m, five minutes to solve, against 28%/9% at h = 0.02 m -- convergence is real but not tight enough for a 2%/1% gate at a size this suite can afford; D7 shows the same story one order lower). Every line below this comment except the mesher and the probe point is otherwise byte-for-byte lame-3d-revolve-hex20.json.
